newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch central bank allocates extra liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Dutch central bank allocates extra liquidity.

text.p: The Dutch central bank offered an extra advances pact on top of the running facility on Friday as call rates were under too much upward pressure. Dealers said the market was desperate for more liquidity.
The central bank topped up Thursday's allocation of 3.0 billion guilders with a further 1.3 billion guilders on Friday.
On Thursday dealers said the allocation of 3.0 was too tight and that they had been expecting at least 4.0 billion guilders under the current seven-day advances pact.
"The problem is solved with the extra allocation," said one dealer. Call rates started coming down after the new pact.
The central bank said it had offered an extra facility under the current pact because unexpected tax payments were squeezing the market and tight liquidity was causing problems for commercial banks.

A money market dealer said call money was likely to slip further on the extra allocation after it fell to bid rates of between 2.68 and 2.75 percent mid-morning from 2.87 to 3.0 percent bid on Thursday.
Dealers said activity in the market had picked up on the extra allocation, but was not unusually high for a Friday.
Three-month deposits were bid at an unchanged 2.92 percent.
One-year paper rose four basis points to 3.18 percent bid.
"Some foreign banks are pushing up the rate for one-year paper and other longer-dated deposits," said another dealer adding foreign players were willing to settle at 3.22 percent.
"The one or two Japanse banks involved have pushed the rate up," said the dealer, but added he did not see it as a trend.
The guilder was trading at 112.10 per 100 marks from 112.11 on Thursday.
